FINDING_ID: MM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` does not enforce the documented same-`flaw_class` requirement for equivalence classes. The documented relation is “same flaw class and `sim >= tau_sim`”, but the code unions findings whenever similarity alone exceeds the threshold. Because `_finding_similarity()` can return `1.0` for textually identical findings even when `flaw_class` differs, the code can merge different flaw classes into one class and then label the merged class with `members[0].flaw_class`. That changes per-class counts and contaminates class-specific convergence math.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Require `findings[i].flaw_class == findings[j].flaw_class` before `union(i, j)`, or bake the class-equality condition directly into the equivalence predicate and document that exact relation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.81  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix’s formal stop rule in §7.4 is `stop_valid(t) = (V̂_remaining(t) < ε) ∧ ¬ascending_abstraction(t)`, but `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop()` implements a different rule: `(smoothed_mu < tau_mu OR smoothed_novelty < tau_novelty_stop OR vocab_saturated) AND abstraction_ok`. The code can therefore stop on novelty-rate or vocabulary heuristics even when the formal online value estimator would not recommend stopping. This is a model/code mismatch, not just a parameter tweak.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either make `stop()` use the appendix’s `V̂_remaining` criterion directly, or formally promote novelty-rate and vocabulary saturation to named appendix extensions instead of presenting them as the same mathematical stop rule.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: `aggregate_per_model_mu()` changes the decision quantity from composite system value to “best surviving model” value by taking `max` over per-model marginal values. The appendix’s `Y(t)` and `V̂(t,T)` are system-level quantities derived from total cognitive yield, not argmax-over-agents quantities. A single model with small positive `mu` can therefore block stopping even when total composite value is exhausted or falling.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base stopping on system-level composite yield/value consistent with `Y(t)` and `V̂(t,T)`. If the “continue while any model is still valuable” rule is desired operationally, define it as a separate conservative heuristic rather than as the appendix implementation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix uses `Δ̄` in §7.5 as a mean across model pairs inside `S_sync`, but §7.6 explicitly says the derived scalar `Δ̄(A→B)` “should not be used for cross-pairing comparison” because the opportunity sets differ across pairings. Averaging `Δ̄(A→B)` over pairs is exactly the cross-pair use that §7.6 forbids, so the sycophancy metric is internally self-contradictory.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the raw mean of pairwise `Δ̄` with an opportunity-weighted pooled statistic, or keep `S_sync` pair-specific and aggregate only after defining a valid weighting scheme.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.validate_k1()` does not actually test the claimed `K=1` reduction. The validator cycles `flaw_class` with `i % 3`, so the synthetic data contains three flaw classes, not one. Its final assertion (`kappa_set(2) > 0.8`) therefore cannot certify the single-class reduction property it claims to validate.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rebuild the validator with a constant `flaw_class` and assert the specific single-class reduction behavior, not just “high convergence” on repeated data.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 3  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix reuses `α`, `β`, and `γ` for unrelated quantities without disambiguation. `β` is the Duane shape parameter in §7.1 but also the HARD-constraint coefficient inside `H(x)` in §7.2; `γ` is the convergence parameter `1−β` in §7.1 but also the cross-module coefficient in `G(x)` in §7.2; `α` is the HIL expertise-floor coefficient in §6 and also an `H(x)` weight in §7.2. This makes several formulas notation-ambiguous and the notation summary incomplete.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rename the `H(x)` coefficients to distinct symbols such as `α_H, β_H, γ_H, δ_H` and update the notation summary accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
